gen_assessment.reasoning: Combines several elements: upper lip swelling and weird sensation after prawn soup are supported by multiple gold HPI facts, but it is phrased as the chief complaint and omits the 1-hour duration from the gold CC. Content is largely supported but not an exact rendering of the gold CC.

Gold hpi-001 and hpi-003 indicate swelling began after prawn soup, about 30 minutes later, and is localized to the upper lip with increasing swelling. Generated hpi-001 reflects ~30 minutes post ingestion, upper lip, and ongoing enlargement.

Gold hpi-004 (throat closing) and hpi-005 (chest tightness with difficulty breathing) support the generated triad of shortness of breath, throat tightness, and chest discomfort. These are restatements of the same symptoms.
Gold facts do not mention whether antihistamines were available at symptom onset. This is new information, neither supported nor contradicted.
Gold facts do not describe whether the patient was alone at onset or when the mother arrived. This is new social context not present in the gold set.
Directly supported by gold pmh-001, which states the patient suffers from asthma.

Gold allergy-001 confirms peanut allergy and having an injection as a child. However, the generated fact adds that this was an anaphylaxis episode with an ED visit, which is not stated in the gold facts. Thus, partially supported but includes additional unverified detail, so classified as ADDITION.
Gold med-001: currently on salbutamol inhalers. Generated: uses a salbutamol inhaler. Same medication use.
Gold facts do not mention occasional antihistamine use nor that the type is unknown. This is additional drug history information.

Gold asm-001: suspected anaphylactic reaction. Generated asm-001 states the same, adding likely trigger (prawn/seafood) and background atopy/anaphylaxis, which is consistent with other gold info (prawn soup, peanut allergy) but is partially additional detail.
Gold plan-002: advised Mom to call the ambulance as a 999 call. Generated plan-001: advise immediate ambulance (999) call. Core recommendation is the same, though the actor (mother) is not specified.

Gold plan-001: advised that patient use an antihistamine straight away. Generated: take available antihistamines while awaiting EMS; this matches immediate antihistamine administration with minor contextual addition (awaiting EMS).
Ensuring a companion is present until ambulance arrival is not mentioned in any gold plan or other section. This is an added safety recommendation.
